title: Scope
test: Has the entity documented, per AI system, whether the AI Act applies and in which role (provider, deployer, importer, distributor, authorised representative)?
recommendation: Maintain an obligations register mapping each AI system to the laws and standards that apply to it, with an owner responsible for horizon scanning.

title: Scope
test: Where an exclusion is relied on, is the reasoning recorded and approved?
recommendation: Maintain an obligations register mapping each AI system to the laws and standards that apply to it, with an owner responsible for horizon scanning.

title: AI literacy
test: Is AI literacy training provided to staff who build, operate or use AI systems, proportionate to their role and the context of use?
note: Training delivered to the data science team only
recommendation: Roll out role-based AI literacy training (all staff, operators, developers, leadership) and track completion.

title: AI literacy
test: Are training content and completion recorded so the measures can be demonstrated?
note: Training delivered to the data science team only
recommendation: Roll out role-based AI literacy training (all staff, operators, developers, leadership) and track completion.

title: Prohibited AI practices
test: Has every AI system been screened against each Art. 5 prohibited practice, with the outcome recorded?

title: Prohibited AI practices
test: Does policy expressly forbid prohibited practices, and is there a control that stops such use cases before development or procurement?

title: Classification rules for high-risk AI systems
test: Is every AI system classified against Annex I and Annex III, with the rationale documented?

title: Classification rules for high-risk AI systems
test: Where the Art. 6(3) "no significant risk" derogation is used, is the assessment documented before market placement and made available on request (and the system registered under Art. 49(2))?

title: Compliance with the requirements
test: High-risk AI systems comply with the Section 2 requirements, taking into account their intended purpose and the generally acknowledged state of the art; where the product is also covered by Annex I legislation, compliance processes may be integrated.

title: Risk management system
test: Is a documented risk management system in place for each high-risk system and run across its lifecycle, with regular systematic review?

title: Risk management system
test: Are known and reasonably foreseeable risks to health, safety and fundamental rights identified, estimated and evaluated, including under reasonably foreseeable misuse and using post-market monitoring data?

title: Risk management system
test: Are risk management measures adopted so that residual risk is judged acceptable, and is residual risk communicated to deployers?

title: Risk management system
test: Is the system tested against prior defined metrics and probabilistic thresholds before market placement, including in real-world conditions where appropriate?

title: Risk management system
test: Is the impact on persons under 18 and other vulnerable groups specifically considered?

title: Data and data governance
test: Do documented data governance practices cover design choices, data collection and origin, preparation (annotation, labelling, cleaning), assumptions, and an assessment of availability and suitability?
recommendation: Produce a datasheet for every dataset used in AI development (source, licence, preparation, known gaps), and add automated data-quality checks and versioning.

title: Data and data governance
test: Are data sets examined for possible biases likely to affect health, safety or fundamental rights or lead to discrimination, with measures to detect, prevent and mitigate them?
recommendation: Produce a datasheet for every dataset used in AI development (source, licence, preparation, known gaps), and add automated data-quality checks and versioning.

title: Data and data governance
test: Are data sets relevant, sufficiently representative, as free of errors and complete as possible, and do they reflect the geographical, contextual and behavioural setting of use?
recommendation: Produce a datasheet for every dataset used in AI development (source, licence, preparation, known gaps), and add automated data-quality checks and versioning.

title: Data and data governance
test: Where special-category personal data is processed for bias detection, are the strict Art. 10(5) conditions and safeguards met and documented?
recommendation: Produce a datasheet for every dataset used in AI development (source, licence, preparation, known gaps), and add automated data-quality checks and versioning.

title: Technical documentation
test: Does technical documentation exist for each high-risk system covering the Annex IV elements (description, development process, monitoring and control, metrics, risk management, changes, standards applied, declaration of conformity, post-market monitoring plan)?

title: Technical documentation
test: Is the documentation completed before market placement and updated with each change?

title: Record-keeping
test: Does each high-risk system automatically log events relevant to identifying risk situations and substantial modifications, post-market monitoring and deployer monitoring?
recommendation: Log inputs, outputs, model version and human interventions for each decision, with tamper-evident storage and a defined retention period.

title: Record-keeping
test: For remote biometric identification systems, do logs record period of use, reference database, input data matched and the persons verifying results?
recommendation: Log inputs, outputs, model version and human interventions for each decision, with tamper-evident storage and a defined retention period.

title: Transparency and provision of information to deployers
test: Do instructions for use state the provider's identity, the system's characteristics, capabilities and limitations, intended purpose, accuracy and robustness metrics, known risks, and conditions affecting performance?
recommendation: Publish instructions for use for each system stating capabilities, limitations, intended and prohibited uses, and oversight expectations.

title: Transparency and provision of information to deployers
test: Do they describe human oversight measures, required computational resources, expected lifetime, maintenance, and how to collect and interpret logs?
recommendation: Publish instructions for use for each system stating capabilities, limitations, intended and prohibited uses, and oversight expectations.

title: Human oversight
test: Are oversight measures identified and either built into the system or specified for the deployer to implement?
recommendation: Define the oversight model for each system (who reviews what, when), build override and stop mechanisms, and train reviewers on automation bias.

title: Human oversight
test: Can overseers understand capacities and limitations, detect anomalies, stay aware of automation bias, and correctly interpret output?
recommendation: Define the oversight model for each system (who reviews what, when), build override and stop mechanisms, and train reviewers on automation bias.

title: Human oversight
test: Can overseers decide not to use the system, disregard, override or reverse output, and interrupt it through a stop procedure that brings it to a safe state?
recommendation: Define the oversight model for each system (who reviews what, when), build override and stop mechanisms, and train reviewers on automation bias.

title: Human oversight
test: For Annex III point 1(a) biometric identification, is any action based on the result verified by at least two competent persons?
recommendation: Define the oversight model for each system (who reviews what, when), build override and stop mechanisms, and train reviewers on automation bias.

title: Accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity
test: Are accuracy levels and metrics declared in the instructions for use and verified by testing?
recommendation: Define metrics and release thresholds per system, automate evaluation in CI, and retain signed-off test reports.

title: Accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity
test: Is the system resilient to errors, faults and inconsistencies (technical redundancy, fail-safe plans), and are feedback loops in continuously learning systems mitigated?
recommendation: Define metrics and release thresholds per system, automate evaluation in CI, and retain signed-off test reports.

title: Accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity
test: Is the system protected against AI-specific attacks such as data poisoning, model poisoning, adversarial examples, model evasion and confidentiality attacks?
recommendation: Define metrics and release thresholds per system, automate evaluation in CI, and retain signed-off test reports.

title: Obligations of providers of high-risk AI systems
test: Is the provider's name, registered trade name or trademark and contact address indicated on the system, its packaging or documentation?
recommendation: Plan the conformity assessment route for each high-risk system, prepare the declaration of conformity and register the system before placing it on the market.

title: Obligations of providers of high-risk AI systems
test: Is there a tracked plan showing each provider obligation (QMS, documentation, logs, conformity assessment, declaration, CE marking, registration, corrective action, accessibility) is met for every high-risk system?
recommendation: Plan the conformity assessment route for each high-risk system, prepare the declaration of conformity and register the system before placing it on the market.

title: Quality management system
test: Does the QMS cover a regulatory compliance strategy (including management of modifications), design and development control, quality assurance, and test and validation procedures?
recommendation: Draft and adopt an AI policy covering scope, principles, risk appetite, prohibited uses and review cadence; obtain executive or board approval.

title: Quality management system
test: Does it cover technical specifications and standards, data management, risk management, post-market monitoring, serious incident reporting, and communication with authorities and customers?
recommendation: Draft and adopt an AI policy covering scope, principles, risk appetite, prohibited uses and review cadence; obtain executive or board approval.

title: Quality management system
test: Does it cover record-keeping, resource management (including security of supply) and an accountability framework defining management and staff responsibilities?
recommendation: Draft and adopt an AI policy covering scope, principles, risk appetite, prohibited uses and review cadence; obtain executive or board approval.

title: Documentation keeping
test: For ten years after the system is placed on the market, providers keep the technical documentation, QMS documentation, notified body approvals and decisions, and the EU declaration of conformity available to authorities.
recommendation: Create a model/system card for each AI system covering intended purpose, architecture, data, metrics and limitations, and keep it under version control with the code.

title: Automatically generated logs
test: Providers keep the automatically generated logs under their control for a period appropriate to the intended purpose, of at least six months unless other law provides otherwise.
recommendation: Log inputs, outputs, model version and human interventions for each decision, with tamper-evident storage and a defined retention period.

title: Corrective actions and duty of information
test: Is there a procedure to correct, withdraw, disable or recall a non-conforming high-risk system without delay?
recommendation: Define suspension and decommissioning criteria and a retirement procedure covering model, data and user communication.

title: Corrective actions and duty of information
test: Does the procedure require informing the value chain and, where a risk exists, the competent authorities and notified body?
recommendation: Define suspension and decommissioning criteria and a retirement procedure covering model, data and user communication.

title: Cooperation with competent authorities
test: On a reasoned request, providers give competent authorities all information and documentation needed to demonstrate conformity, in an easily understood language, and access to logs under their control.
recommendation: Maintain an obligations register mapping each AI system to the laws and standards that apply to it, with an owner responsible for horizon scanning.

title: Authorised representatives of providers of high-risk AI systems
test: A provider established outside the EU appoints, by written mandate, an authorised representative established in the EU before making a high-risk system available, empowered to verify documentation, keep records for ten years, provide information and cooperate with authorities.

title: Obligations of importers
test: Is there a pre-market verification checklist covering conformity assessment, technical documentation, CE marking, declaration of conformity, instructions for use and authorised representative?

title: Obligations of importers
test: Are non-conforming systems blocked from the market, and are importer details and records kept for ten years?

title: Obligations of distributors
test: Before making a high-risk system available, distributors verify CE marking, declaration of conformity and instructions, and that provider and importer obligations were met; they withhold or correct non-conforming systems and cooperate with authorities.

title: Responsibilities along the AI value chain
test: Has the entity checked whether rebranding, substantial modification or a change of intended purpose makes it the provider of any high-risk system?
recommendation: Add AI-specific due diligence to procurement and contract clauses covering documentation, permitted use, audit rights, incident notice and model change notification.

title: Responsibilities along the AI value chain
test: Are there written agreements with suppliers of tools, services, components or models integrated into high-risk systems, specifying information, capabilities, technical access and assistance?
recommendation: Add AI-specific due diligence to procurement and contract clauses covering documentation, permitted use, audit rights, incident notice and model change notification.

title: Obligations of deployers of high-risk AI systems
test: Are technical and organisational measures in place to use each high-risk system in accordance with its instructions for use?
recommendation: Define the oversight model for each system (who reviews what, when), build override and stop mechanisms, and train reviewers on automation bias.

title: Obligations of deployers of high-risk AI systems
test: Is human oversight assigned to persons with the necessary competence, training, authority and support?
recommendation: Define the oversight model for each system (who reviews what, when), build override and stop mechanisms, and train reviewers on automation bias.

title: Obligations of deployers of high-risk AI systems
test: Where the deployer controls input data, is it relevant and sufficiently representative for the intended purpose?
recommendation: Define the oversight model for each system (who reviews what, when), build override and stop mechanisms, and train reviewers on automation bias.

title: Obligations of deployers of high-risk AI systems
test: Is operation monitored, with the provider and authorities informed and use suspended where a risk or serious incident arises?
recommendation: Define the oversight model for each system (who reviews what, when), build override and stop mechanisms, and train reviewers on automation bias.

title: Obligations of deployers of high-risk AI systems
test: Are logs under the deployer's control kept for at least six months?
recommendation: Define the oversight model for each system (who reviews what, when), build override and stop mechanisms, and train reviewers on automation bias.

title: Obligations of deployers of high-risk AI systems
test: Before workplace use, are workers' representatives and affected workers informed?
recommendation: Define the oversight model for each system (who reviews what, when), build override and stop mechanisms, and train reviewers on automation bias.

title: Obligations of deployers of high-risk AI systems
test: Are natural persons subject to Annex III decisions informed that a high-risk AI system is used?
recommendation: Define the oversight model for each system (who reviews what, when), build override and stop mechanisms, and train reviewers on automation bias.

title: Fundamental rights impact assessment for high-risk AI systems
test: Was a FRIA completed before first use, describing the deployer's processes, period and frequency of use, categories of persons affected, specific risks of harm, human oversight measures, and measures if risks materialise (including governance and complaints)?
recommendation: Adopt a combined AI/data-protection/fundamental-rights impact assessment template and require a completed assessment before go-live and on material change.

title: Fundamental rights impact assessment for high-risk AI systems
test: Has the market surveillance authority been notified of the results, and is the FRIA updated when relevant elements change?
recommendation: Adopt a combined AI/data-protection/fundamental-rights impact assessment template and require a completed assessment before go-live and on material change.

title: Conformity assessment
test: Has the applicable conformity assessment route been determined and completed for each high-risk system before market placement?
recommendation: Plan the conformity assessment route for each high-risk system, prepare the declaration of conformity and register the system before placing it on the market.

title: Conformity assessment
test: Does change management trigger a new conformity assessment on substantial modification?
recommendation: Plan the conformity assessment route for each high-risk system, prepare the declaration of conformity and register the system before placing it on the market.

title: EU declaration of conformity
test: Providers draw up a written, machine-readable, signed EU declaration of conformity for each high-risk system containing the Annex V information, keep it for ten years and keep it up to date.
recommendation: Plan the conformity assessment route for each high-risk system, prepare the declaration of conformity and register the system before placing it on the market.

title: CE marking
test: CE marking is affixed visibly, legibly and indelibly (digitally for digital-only systems), followed by the notified body's identification number where applicable.
recommendation: Plan the conformity assessment route for each high-risk system, prepare the declaration of conformity and register the system before placing it on the market.

title: Registration
test: Before placing an Annex III high-risk system on the market, the provider registers itself and the system in the EU database; providers relying on the Art. 6(3) derogation also register; public-authority deployers register their use.
recommendation: Plan the conformity assessment route for each high-risk system, prepare the declaration of conformity and register the system before placing it on the market.

title: Transparency obligations for providers and deployers of certain AI systems
test: Are people informed that they are interacting with an AI system, unless obvious from context?
recommendation: Add clear AI-interaction notices at the point of use and label or watermark AI-generated content.

title: Transparency obligations for providers and deployers of certain AI systems
test: Are synthetic audio, image, video or text outputs marked in a machine-readable format and detectable as artificially generated?
recommendation: Add clear AI-interaction notices at the point of use and label or watermark AI-generated content.

title: Transparency obligations for providers and deployers of certain AI systems
test: Are deep fakes, and AI-generated text published to inform the public on matters of public interest, disclosed as artificially generated or manipulated (unless under human editorial responsibility)?
recommendation: Add clear AI-interaction notices at the point of use and label or watermark AI-generated content.

title: Transparency obligations for providers and deployers of certain AI systems
test: Are persons exposed to emotion recognition or biometric categorisation informed of its operation?
recommendation: Add clear AI-interaction notices at the point of use and label or watermark AI-generated content.

title: Transparency obligations for providers and deployers of certain AI systems
test: Is the information given clearly and distinguishably at the latest at the first interaction or exposure, meeting accessibility requirements?
recommendation: Add clear AI-interaction notices at the point of use and label or watermark AI-generated content.

title: Classification of general-purpose AI models as general-purpose AI models with systemic risk
test: The provider assesses whether its general-purpose AI model has high-impact capabilities (presumed above 10^25 FLOPs of cumulative training compute) or has been designated by the Commission as presenting systemic risk.

title: Procedure
test: The provider notifies the Commission without delay, and within two weeks, once its model meets or is known to meet the systemic-risk threshold, and may argue the model does not present systemic risk.

title: Obligations for providers of general-purpose AI models
test: Is technical documentation (Annex XI), including training and testing process and evaluation results, kept up to date and available to the AI Office?

title: Obligations for providers of general-purpose AI models
test: Is information and documentation (Annex XII) available to downstream providers integrating the model?

title: Obligations for providers of general-purpose AI models
test: Is there a policy to comply with EU copyright law, including identifying and honouring text-and-data-mining rights reservations?

title: Obligations for providers of general-purpose AI models
test: Has a sufficiently detailed summary of training content been published using the AI Office template?

title: Authorised representatives of providers of general-purpose AI models
test: A GPAI model provider established outside the EU appoints an EU authorised representative by written mandate before placing the model on the market.

title: Obligations of providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk
test: Are model evaluations, including documented adversarial testing, performed with standardised protocols?

title: Obligations of providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk
test: Are possible systemic risks at Union level assessed and mitigated, including their sources?

title: Obligations of providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk
test: Are serious incidents and corrective measures tracked, documented and reported to the AI Office and national authorities without undue delay?

title: Obligations of providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk
test: Is an adequate level of cybersecurity ensured for the model and its physical infrastructure?

title: Codes of practice
test: The provider has decided whether to rely on the general-purpose AI code of practice to demonstrate compliance, or documented alternative adequate means of compliance.

title: Testing of high-risk AI systems in real world conditions outside AI regulatory sandboxes
test: Was a real-world testing plan submitted to and approved by the market surveillance authority, and the test registered with an EU-wide identification number?

title: Testing of high-risk AI systems in real world conditions outside AI regulatory sandboxes
test: Is testing limited in duration (six months, extendable once), with vulnerable groups protected, effective oversight, and predictions or decisions able to be reversed or disregarded?

title: Testing of high-risk AI systems in real world conditions outside AI regulatory sandboxes
test: Are serious incidents during testing reported, and can subjects withdraw at any time?

title: Informed consent to participate in testing in real world conditions outside AI regulatory sandboxes
test: Freely given informed consent is obtained from test subjects before participation, covering the nature and objectives of testing, duration, their rights including withdrawal without detriment, and how to request reversal; consent is dated, documented and a copy given.

title: Post-market monitoring by providers and post-market monitoring plan for high-risk AI systems
test: Is there a post-market monitoring plan for each high-risk system, part of its technical documentation?
recommendation: Deploy production monitoring for performance, drift and fairness with alert thresholds, owners and documented response playbooks.

title: Post-market monitoring by providers and post-market monitoring plan for high-risk AI systems
test: Is performance data (from deployers or other sources) actively collected and analysed to evaluate continuous compliance?
recommendation: Deploy production monitoring for performance, drift and fairness with alert thresholds, owners and documented response playbooks.

title: Reporting of serious incidents
test: Does the incident procedure define "serious incident" and the 15-day, 10-day and 2-day reporting deadlines?
recommendation: Extend the incident process to AI harms and malfunctions, with severity criteria, regulator notification deadlines and post-incident review.

title: Reporting of serious incidents
test: Does it require investigation, risk assessment and corrective action while preserving evidence?
recommendation: Extend the incident process to AI harms and malfunctions, with severity criteria, regulator notification deadlines and post-incident review.

title: Right to explanation of individual decision-making
test: A person affected by a decision based on the output of an Annex III high-risk system that has legal or similarly significant effects can obtain from the deployer clear and meaningful explanations of the role of the AI system in the decision and the main elements of the decision.
recommendation: Implement explanation methods suited to each model and a process to give affected individuals the main reasons for a decision.

title: Reporting of infringements and protection of reporting persons
test: Internal reporting channels cover infringements of the AI Act and protect reporting persons in line with Directive (EU) 2019/1937.
recommendation: Establish an AI governance committee with a named accountable executive, assign an owner to every AI system, and publish a RACI with escalation and concern-reporting routes.

title: Codes of conduct for voluntary application of specific requirements
test: For AI systems that are not high-risk, the entity has considered voluntarily applying high-risk requirements or a code of conduct (for example on sustainability, accessibility, inclusive design and AI literacy).

title: AI systems already placed on the market or put into service and general-purpose AI models already placed on the market
test: The entity has identified AI systems and GPAI models placed on the market or put into service before the application dates, and the transitional deadlines and significant-change triggers that apply to them.
recommendation: Maintain an obligations register mapping each AI system to the laws and standards that apply to it, with an owner responsible for horizon scanning.

title: Principles relating to processing of personal data
test: Are the purposes of each AI processing activity (training, fine-tuning, inference, monitoring) specified, and is further use checked for compatibility?
recommendation: Record the lawful basis or consent for each AI processing purpose, update privacy notices, and apply minimisation, retention limits and pseudonymisation to training and inference data.

title: Principles relating to processing of personal data
test: Is data minimised for training and inference, with retention periods set and enforced?
recommendation: Record the lawful basis or consent for each AI processing purpose, update privacy notices, and apply minimisation, retention limits and pseudonymisation to training and inference data.

title: Principles relating to processing of personal data
test: Are steps taken to keep personal data, including AI-generated inferences about people, accurate?
recommendation: Record the lawful basis or consent for each AI processing purpose, update privacy notices, and apply minimisation, retention limits and pseudonymisation to training and inference data.

title: Principles relating to processing of personal data
test: Can the controller demonstrate compliance with each principle (accountability documentation)?
recommendation: Record the lawful basis or consent for each AI processing purpose, update privacy notices, and apply minimisation, retention limits and pseudonymisation to training and inference data.

title: Lawfulness of processing
test: Is a lawful basis identified and recorded for each AI processing purpose?
note: Covered by the group privacy programme
recommendation: Record the lawful basis or consent for each AI processing purpose, update privacy notices, and apply minimisation, retention limits and pseudonymisation to training and inference data.

title: Lawfulness of processing
test: Where legitimate interests is relied on (for example for model training), is a documented balancing test in place?
note: Covered by the group privacy programme
recommendation: Record the lawful basis or consent for each AI processing purpose, update privacy notices, and apply minimisation, retention limits and pseudonymisation to training and inference data.

title: Lawfulness of processing
test: Where data is reused for a new purpose, is the Art. 6(4) compatibility assessment documented?
note: Covered by the group privacy programme
recommendation: Record the lawful basis or consent for each AI processing purpose, update privacy notices, and apply minimisation, retention limits and pseudonymisation to training and inference data.

title: Conditions for consent
test: Where consent is relied on, the controller can demonstrate it, the request is distinguishable and plain, consent is freely given, and withdrawal is as easy as giving it.
recommendation: Record the lawful basis or consent for each AI processing purpose, update privacy notices, and apply minimisation, retention limits and pseudonymisation to training and inference data.

title: Conditions applicable to child's consent in relation to information society services
test: For online services offered directly to children below the national age of digital consent (16, or as low as 13), consent is given or authorised by the holder of parental responsibility, with reasonable verification efforts.

title: Processing of special categories of personal data
test: Is an Art. 9(2) condition identified and documented for each AI processing of special-category data, including inferred data?

title: Processing of special categories of personal data
test: Are additional safeguards (access restrictions, pseudonymisation, purpose separation) applied?

title: Processing of personal data relating to criminal convictions and offences
test: Criminal-offence data is processed only under official authority or where authorised by Union or Member State law providing appropriate safeguards.

title: Transparent information, communication and modalities for the exercise of the rights of the data subject
test: Information and communications are concise, transparent, intelligible and in plain language; rights requests are answered without undue delay and within one month (extendable by two months), free of charge, with identity verified.
recommendation: Extend the rights-request procedure to AI systems (including training data and model outputs) and define safeguards for solely automated decisions.

title: Information to be provided where personal data are collected from the data subject
test: Do privacy notices describe each AI processing purpose, lawful basis, recipients, retention and rights?
recommendation: Record the lawful basis or consent for each AI processing purpose, update privacy notices, and apply minimisation, retention limits and pseudonymisation to training and inference data.

title: Information to be provided where personal data are collected from the data subject
test: Where automated decision-making or profiling occurs, do notices explain the logic involved and its significance and consequences?
recommendation: Record the lawful basis or consent for each AI processing purpose, update privacy notices, and apply minimisation, retention limits and pseudonymisation to training and inference data.

title: Information to be provided where personal data have not been obtained from the data subject
test: Where personal data is obtained indirectly (for example third-party or publicly scraped training data), people are informed within a reasonable period (at most one month), including the source; or the disproportionate-effort exemption is assessed and documented with protective measures such as public information.
recommendation: Produce a datasheet for every dataset used in AI development (source, licence, preparation, known gaps), and add automated data-quality checks and versioning.

title: Right of access by the data subject
test: People can obtain confirmation of processing, a copy of their data, and information on purposes, recipients, retention, source, and the existence and logic of automated decision-making.
recommendation: Extend the rights-request procedure to AI systems (including training data and model outputs) and define safeguards for solely automated decisions.

title: Right to rectification
test: Inaccurate personal data, including in AI-derived profiles and outputs, can be rectified without undue delay and incomplete data completed.
recommendation: Extend the rights-request procedure to AI systems (including training data and model outputs) and define safeguards for solely automated decisions.

title: Right to erasure ('right to be forgotten')
test: Erasure requests are handled where grounds apply, with a documented approach for personal data in training data sets and derived models.
recommendation: Extend the rights-request procedure to AI systems (including training data and model outputs) and define safeguards for solely automated decisions.

title: Right to restriction of processing
test: Processing can be restricted (for example while accuracy is contested), and restricted data is marked and not used for AI processing.
recommendation: Extend the rights-request procedure to AI systems (including training data and model outputs) and define safeguards for solely automated decisions.

title: Notification obligation regarding rectification or erasure of personal data or restriction of processing
test: Rectification, erasure or restriction is communicated to each recipient of the data unless impossible or disproportionate.
recommendation: Extend the rights-request procedure to AI systems (including training data and model outputs) and define safeguards for solely automated decisions.

title: Right to data portability
test: Where processing is automated and based on consent or contract, people can receive their data in a structured, commonly used, machine-readable format and transmit it to another controller.
recommendation: Extend the rights-request procedure to AI systems (including training data and model outputs) and define safeguards for solely automated decisions.

title: Right to object
test: People can object to processing based on legitimate interests or public task (including profiling), processing stops unless compelling grounds are shown, objection to direct marketing is absolute, and the right is presented at the first communication.
recommendation: Extend the rights-request procedure to AI systems (including training data and model outputs) and define safeguards for solely automated decisions.

title: Automated individual decision-making, including profiling
test: Has the entity identified every decision based solely on automated processing with legal or similarly significant effects?
recommendation: Provide an appeal channel with human review and a correction route for every consequential AI-assisted decision.

title: Automated individual decision-making, including profiling
test: Does each such decision rely on an Art. 22(2) exception (contract necessity, authorised by law, or explicit consent)?
recommendation: Provide an appeal channel with human review and a correction route for every consequential AI-assisted decision.

title: Automated individual decision-making, including profiling
test: Can people obtain human intervention, express their point of view and contest the decision?
recommendation: Provide an appeal channel with human review and a correction route for every consequential AI-assisted decision.

title: Automated individual decision-making, including profiling
test: Is special-category data excluded unless Art. 9(2)(a) or (g) applies with safeguards?
recommendation: Provide an appeal channel with human review and a correction route for every consequential AI-assisted decision.

title: Responsibility of the controller
test: The controller implements appropriate technical and organisational measures, including data protection policies, to ensure and demonstrate compliance, and reviews them.
recommendation: Draft and adopt an AI policy covering scope, principles, risk appetite, prohibited uses and review cadence; obtain executive or board approval.

title: Data protection by design and by default
test: Data protection principles are built into the design of AI systems (for example pseudonymisation, minimisation, access limits), and by default only data necessary for each purpose is processed.
recommendation: Record the lawful basis or consent for each AI processing purpose, update privacy notices, and apply minimisation, retention limits and pseudonymisation to training and inference data.

title: Joint controllers
test: Where the entity jointly determines purposes and means with another party (for example an AI partner), a transparent arrangement allocates responsibilities, and its essence is available to data subjects.
recommendation: Add AI-specific due diligence to procurement and contract clauses covering documentation, permitted use, audit rights, incident notice and model change notification.

title: Representatives of controllers or processors not established in the Union
test: A controller or processor outside the EU that is subject to the GDPR designates in writing a representative in the EU.

title: Processor
test: Are AI and cloud vendors processing personal data covered by contracts with the Art. 28(3) terms?
recommendation: Add AI-specific due diligence to procurement and contract clauses covering documentation, permitted use, audit rights, incident notice and model change notification.

title: Processor
test: Do contracts restrict the vendor from using the entity's data to train or improve its own models unless agreed?
recommendation: Add AI-specific due diligence to procurement and contract clauses covering documentation, permitted use, audit rights, incident notice and model change notification.

title: Processing under the authority of the controller or processor
test: Staff and processors process personal data only on the controller's instructions.

test: System requirements are elicited from and understood by relevant AI actors, and design decisions take socio-technical implications into account to address AI risks.

title: Tasks and methods defined
test: The specific tasks and methods used to implement the tasks that the AI system will support are defined.

title: Knowledge limits and human use of output
test: Information about the AI system's knowledge limits and how system output may be utilized and overseen by humans is documented.
recommendation: Create a model/system card for each AI system covering intended purpose, architecture, data, metrics and limitations, and keep it under version control with the code.

title: Scientific integrity and TEVV
test: Scientific integrity and TEVV considerations are identified and documented, including those related to experimental design, data collection and selection, system trustworthiness, and construct validation.
recommendation: Produce a datasheet for every dataset used in AI development (source, licence, preparation, known gaps), and add automated data-quality checks and versioning.

title: Benefits documented
test: Potential benefits of intended AI system functionality and performance are examined and documented.
recommendation: Adopt a combined AI/data-protection/fundamental-rights impact assessment template and require a completed assessment before go-live and on material change.

title: Costs of errors documented
test: Potential costs, including non-monetary costs, which result from expected or realized AI errors or system functionality and trustworthiness are examined and documented.
recommendation: Adopt a combined AI/data-protection/fundamental-rights impact assessment template and require a completed assessment before go-live and on material change.

title: Application scope
test: Targeted application scope is specified and documented based on the system's capability, established context, and AI system categorization.

title: Operator proficiency
test: Processes for operator and practitioner proficiency with AI system performance and trustworthiness, and relevant technical standards and certifications, are defined, assessed, and documented.
recommendation: Roll out role-based AI literacy training (all staff, operators, developers, leadership) and track completion.

title: Human oversight processes
test: Processes for human oversight are defined, assessed, and documented in accordance with organizational policies.
recommendation: Define the oversight model for each system (who reviews what, when), build override and stop mechanisms, and train reviewers on automation bias.

title: Mapping legal and technology risks of components
test: Approaches for mapping AI technology and legal risks of its components, including the use of third-party data or software, are in place, followed, and documented, as are risks of infringement of a third party's intellectual property or other rights.
recommendation: Add AI-specific due diligence to procurement and contract clauses covering documentation, permitted use, audit rights, incident notice and model change notification.

title: Internal risk controls for components
test: Internal risk controls for components of the AI system, including third-party AI technologies, are identified and documented.
recommendation: Pin and record vendor model versions, re-run your evaluation suite on every model change, and define a fallback for vendor outage or withdrawal.

title: Likelihood and magnitude of impacts
test: Likelihood and magnitude of each identified impact (both potentially beneficial and harmful) based on expected use, past uses of AI systems in similar contexts, public incident reports, feedback from those external to the team, or other data are identified and documented.
recommendation: Implement an AI risk management procedure with a risk register per system, defined scoring, treatment plans, residual-risk sign-off and re-assessment triggers.

title: Engagement with affected actors
test: Practices and personnel for supporting regular engagement with relevant AI actors and integrating feedback about positive, negative, and unanticipated impacts are in place and documented.
recommendation: Provide an appeal channel with human review and a correction route for every consequential AI-assisted decision.

title: Metrics selected
test: Approaches and metrics for measurement of AI risks enumerated during the MAP function are selected for implementation starting with the most significant AI risks. The risks or trustworthiness characteristics that will not or cannot be measured are properly documented.
recommendation: Define metrics and release thresholds per system, automate evaluation in CI, and retain signed-off test reports.

title: Metrics reviewed
test: Appropriateness of AI metrics and effectiveness of existing controls are regularly assessed and updated, including reports of errors and potential impacts on affected communities.
recommendation: Deploy production monitoring for performance, drift and fairness with alert thresholds, owners and documented response playbooks.

title: Independent assessment
test: Internal experts who did not serve as front-line developers for the system and/or independent assessors are involved in regular assessments and updates.
recommendation: Add AI governance to the internal audit plan, hold a periodic management review, and track corrective actions to closure.

title: TEVV documentation
test: Test sets, metrics, and details about the tools used during TEVV are documented.
recommendation: Define metrics and release thresholds per system, automate evaluation in CI, and retain signed-off test reports.

title: Human-subject evaluations
test: Evaluations involving human subjects meet applicable requirements (including human subject protection) and are representative of the relevant population.
recommendation: Define metrics and release thresholds per system, automate evaluation in CI, and retain signed-off test reports.

title: Performance in deployment-like conditions
test: AI system performance or assurance criteria are measured qualitatively or quantitatively and demonstrated for conditions similar to deployment setting(s). Measures are documented.
recommendation: Define metrics and release thresholds per system, automate evaluation in CI, and retain signed-off test reports.

title: Production monitoring
test: The functionality and behavior of the AI system and its components are monitored when in production.
recommendation: Deploy production monitoring for performance, drift and fairness with alert thresholds, owners and documented response playbooks.

title: Validity and reliability
test: The AI system to be deployed is demonstrated to be valid and reliable. Limitations of the generalizability beyond the conditions under which the technology was developed are documented.

title: Safety evaluation
test: The AI system is evaluated regularly for safety risks. The AI system to be deployed is demonstrated to be safe, its residual negative risk does not exceed the risk tolerance, and it can fail safely, particularly if made to operate beyond its knowledge limits.
recommendation: Define metrics and release thresholds per system, automate evaluation in CI, and retain signed-off test reports.

title: Security and resilience
test: AI system security and resilience are evaluated and documented.
recommendation: Threat-model each AI system, run adversarial/red-team testing before release, and harden model, data and pipeline access.

title: Transparency and accountability risks
test: Risks associated with transparency and accountability are examined and documented.
recommendation: Publish instructions for use for each system stating capabilities, limitations, intended and prohibited uses, and oversight expectations.

title: Explainability
test: The AI model is explained, validated, and documented, and AI system output is interpreted within its context to inform responsible use and governance.

title: Privacy risk
test: Privacy risk of the AI system is examined and documented.
recommendation: Record the lawful basis or consent for each AI processing purpose, update privacy notices, and apply minimisation, retention limits and pseudonymisation to training and inference data.

title: Fairness and bias
test: Fairness and bias are evaluated and results are documented.
recommendation: Add group fairness metrics to the evaluation suite, set tolerances, and commission an independent bias audit where the law requires one.

title: Environmental impact
test: Environmental impact and sustainability of AI model training and management activities are assessed and documented.

title: Effectiveness of TEVV
test: Effectiveness of the employed TEVV metrics and processes in the MEASURE function are evaluated and documented.
recommendation: Add AI governance to the internal audit plan, hold a periodic management review, and track corrective actions to closure.

title: Tracking emergent risks
test: Approaches, personnel, and documentation are in place to regularly identify and track existing, unanticipated, and emergent AI risks based on factors such as intended and actual performance in deployed contexts.
recommendation: Deploy production monitoring for performance, drift and fairness with alert thresholds, owners and documented response playbooks.

title: Hard-to-measure risks
test: Risk tracking approaches are considered for settings where AI risks are difficult to assess using currently available measurement techniques or where metrics are not yet available.

title: User feedback and appeal
test: Feedback processes for end users and impacted communities to report problems and appeal system outcomes are established and integrated into AI system evaluation metrics.
recommendation: Provide an appeal channel with human review and a correction route for every consequential AI-assisted decision.

title: Context-informed measurement
test: Measurement approaches for identifying AI risks are connected to deployment context(s) and informed through consultation with domain experts and other end users. Approaches are documented.
recommendation: Define metrics and release thresholds per system, automate evaluation in CI, and retain signed-off test reports.

title: Validated trustworthiness in deployment
test: Measurement results regarding AI system trustworthiness in deployment context(s) and across the AI lifecycle are informed by input from domain experts and relevant AI actors to validate whether the system is performing consistently as intended. Results are documented.
recommendation: Deploy production monitoring for performance, drift and fairness with alert thresholds, owners and documented response playbooks.

title: Measured improvements and declines
test: Measurable performance improvements or declines based on consultations with relevant AI actors, including affected communities, and field data about context-relevant risks and trustworthiness characteristics are identified and documented.
recommendation: Deploy production monitoring for performance, drift and fairness with alert thresholds, owners and documented response playbooks.

title: Go / no-go determination
test: A determination is made as to whether the AI system achieves its intended purposes and stated objectives and whether its development or deployment should proceed.

title: Risk treatment prioritised
test: Treatment of documented AI risks is prioritized based on impact, likelihood, and available resources or methods.

title: Responses to high-priority risks
test: Responses to the AI risks deemed high priority, as identified by the MAP function, are developed, planned, and documented. Risk response options can include mitigating, transferring, avoiding, or accepting.

title: Residual risk documented
test: Negative residual risks (defined as the sum of all unmitigated risks) to both downstream acquirers of AI systems and end users are documented.
recommendation: Implement an AI risk management procedure with a risk register per system, defined scoring, treatment plans, residual-risk sign-off and re-assessment triggers.

title: Resources and non-AI alternatives
test: Resources required to manage AI risks are taken into account along with viable non-AI alternative systems, approaches, or methods to reduce the magnitude or likelihood of potential impacts.

title: Sustaining value
test: Mechanisms are in place and applied to sustain the value of deployed AI systems.
recommendation: Deploy production monitoring for performance, drift and fairness with alert thresholds, owners and documented response playbooks.

title: Responding to unknown risks
test: Procedures are followed to respond to and recover from a previously unknown risk when it is identified.
recommendation: Extend the incident process to AI harms and malfunctions, with severity criteria, regulator notification deadlines and post-incident review.

title: Disengage or deactivate
test: Mechanisms are in place and applied, and responsibilities are assigned and understood, to supersede, disengage, or deactivate AI systems that demonstrate performance or outcomes inconsistent with intended use.
recommendation: Define the oversight model for each system (who reviews what, when), build override and stop mechanisms, and train reviewers on automation bias.

title: Third-party risk monitoring
test: AI risks and benefits from third-party resources are regularly monitored, and risk controls are applied and documented.
recommendation: Add AI-specific due diligence to procurement and contract clauses covering documentation, permitted use, audit rights, incident notice and model change notification.

title: Pre-trained model monitoring
test: Pre-trained models which are used for development are monitored as part of AI system regular monitoring and maintenance.
recommendation: Pin and record vendor model versions, re-run your evaluation suite on every model change, and define a fallback for vendor outage or withdrawal.

title: Post-deployment monitoring plans
test: Post-deployment AI system monitoring plans are implemented, including mechanisms for capturing and evaluating input from users and other relevant AI actors, appeal and override, decommissioning, incident response, recovery, and change management.
recommendation: Deploy production monitoring for performance, drift and fairness with alert thresholds, owners and documented response playbooks.

title: Continual improvement

recommendation: Version models and datasets alongside code, require reviewed and approved changes, and define what counts as a substantial modification that re-triggers assessment.

title: Incident communication and recovery
test: Incidents and errors are communicated to relevant AI actors, including affected communities. Processes for tracking, responding to, and recovering from incidents and errors are followed and documented.
recommendation: Extend the incident process to AI harms and malfunctions, with severity criteria, regulator notification deadlines and post-incident review.
